_meta.posture: findings, never approvals; flag against cited prescriptive tables; never emit a member size; never a 'passes' state (A20). Severity: CODE (adopted prescriptive requirement; never relaxable) / STD (engineering-standard bound) / HEUR (published rule-of-thumb) / CONV (practice convention).
_meta.jurisdiction: US-IRC defaults. Southern-African regimes implemented (A29): pass region= to select. SANS 10400 is LAW only in South Africa (Act 103 of 1977); in Namibia it has force only where a local authority incorporated it under Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992 s 94B, and on communal land there is no building control at all. Severity is therefore jurisdiction-dependent - see _jurisdiction_profiles.
_meta.edition_note: span-table values are the WORST-CASE grade column (a span within them is legal under ANY grade - zero false positives); verify against the locally adopted edition before hardening (recorded follow-up)

_jurisdiction_profiles._note: Resolve the regime BEFORE quoting any requirement. Source: knowledge-base/03_codes_standards/00_overview.md and 04_namibia-building-regulations.md (both status:stable, confidence:high). max_severity caps what any rule may emit here: legal force is jurisdictional, so a rule that is CODE in ZA is at most STD where no code has been adopted.

US.label: United States (IRC)
US.legal_basis: IRC as adopted by the local jurisdiction

ZA.label: South Africa
ZA.legal_basis: National Building Regulations and Building Standards Act 103 of 1977; the SANS 10400 series is the deemed-to-satisfy route. Deemed-to-satisfy is non-mandatory: a rational design by a competent person appointed under Regulation A19 is the lawful alternative.

NA-local-authority.label: Namibia - proclaimed local authority (municipal / town / village council)
NA-local-authority.legal_basis: Namibia has NO national building act. A local authority council may make building regulations under Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992 s 94(1)(ag), and may incorporate SANS by reference under s 94B - but only the standard it actually incorporated, at the edition it incorporated (s 94B(3) blocks automatic edition updates). Unless that council's gazetted regulations have been read, SANS findings here are professional standard of care, NOT law.
NA-local-authority.advisory: Obtain the council's Government Notice number and its s 94B list of incorporated standard publications before treating any SANS value as binding. s 94B(4) entitles you to read an incorporated standard free of charge at the council offices.

NA-settlement.label: Namibia - declared settlement area (Regional Councils Act 22 of 1992)
NA-settlement.legal_basis: A regional council does NOT hold the LAA s 94(1)(ag) building-regulation power (that is a local authority council power). Plan approval in a settlement may be handled administratively, by the responsible ministry, or not at all.
NA-settlement.advisory: Building control in settlements is thin and must be confirmed settlement by settlement.

NA-communal.label: Namibia - communal land (Communal Land Reform Act 5 of 2002)
NA-communal.legal_basis: NO building control regime: no building plan approval, no building control officer, no inspection regime, no occupancy certificate, and SANS 10400 is not law. The right to build comes from a customary land right or leasehold allocated by the Chief or Traditional Authority and ratified/registered by the Communal Land Board.
NA-communal.advisory: No building control is not the same as no obligations: the designer, engineer and builder carry ordinary common-law and professional duties of care, and donor-funded, bank-financed or institutional projects are almost always CONTRACTUALLY required to meet SANS 10400/10160. With no regulator, the specification and the engineer's certification are the only quality control. Environmental clearance, electrical certification, water permits, OHS duties and professional registration DO still apply.

NA-unresolved.label: Namibia - regime NOT yet established
NA-unresolved.legal_basis: Unknown. Namibian building control depends entirely on which of three regimes the site falls in: proclaimed local authority, declared settlement, or communal land.
NA-unresolved.advisory: Resolve the regime before relying on any finding. The proclaimed boundary is not obvious on the ground - obtain the proclamation Government Notice and the surveyed boundary. For Okongo specifically: proclaimed a Village Council in 2015, so inside that boundary it HAS the s 94(1)(ag) power, but whether it has gazetted building regulations is unverified; immediately outside the boundary the land is communal and no building control applies.

joist_span_max_m.source: IRC R502.3.1(2) 40 psf live, worst-case grade column (edition-verify pending)
joist_span_max_m.finding: modeled joist span exceeds the prescriptive envelope of IRC R502.3.1(2); verify with a licensed engineer

concrete_slab_min_depth.source: ACI 318 Table 7.3.1.1 (min thickness unless deflections computed); most lenient column l/28 used as the flag line
concrete_slab_min_depth.finding: slab thinner than span/28 - outside ACI 318's no-deflection-check envelope

concrete_beam_min_depth.source: ACI 318 Table 9.3.1.1; most lenient column l/21
concrete_beam_min_depth.finding: beam shallower than span/21 - outside ACI 318's no-deflection-check envelope

steel_beam_depth.source: Ruddy/AISC economical-depth rule of thumb (~span/20); flag below span/30
steel_beam_depth.finding: steel member depth below span/30 - far outside the economical-depth rule of thumb

header_required.source: IRC R602.7 (headers required over openings in bearing walls) - existence check only, no sizing
header_required.finding: opening in a bearing wall has no header member above it

lintel_bearing_min_mm.finding: lintel end bearing below the standard minimum for its span

masonry_slenderness.finding: masonry wall slenderness exceeds the EC6 limit

masonry_min_thickness_mm.source: US empirical masonry provisions (6 in bearing walls one story / 8 in multi-story)
masonry_min_thickness_mm.finding: bearing masonry thinner than the empirical minimum

footing_width.source: IRC R403.1 (footing at least as wide as the wall; projections per table)
footing_width.finding: footing narrower than the wall it carries

soil_bearing_min_kpa.source: IRC R401.4.1 (presumptive 1,500 psf minimum; below => soils investigation / engineered design)
soil_bearing_min_kpa.finding: declared soil bearing below the presumptive minimum - engineered design required (this is itself the flag)

rafter_tie_topology.source: IRC R802.4.1 / R802.3 (rafters require ceiling joists/rafter ties or a structural ridge)
rafter_tie_topology.finding: rafters without rafter ties, ceiling joists, or a structural ridge member

concrete_tile.source: BS 5534 / manufacturer minima for plain+interlocking tile practice (the Okongo check)

roof_pitch_min_deg.finding: roof pitch below the minimum for its covering

stairs.source: IRC R311.7 (riser <=196 mm, tread >=254 mm, headroom >=2032 mm, width >=914 mm)

sans.source: SANS 10400-M clause 4.2 (riser <=200 mm, going >=250 mm, headroom >=2,1 m from the pitch line, width >=750 mm) - values taken from the 2011 edition per knowledge-base/03_codes_standards/02_sans-10400-parts-register.md; current is Ed. 3.02 (2025), RE-VERIFY before relying on them

blondel.source: SANS 10400-M clause 4.2: going + 2 x riser between 570 mm and 650 mm (a NARROWER band than the generic Blondel convention)

sans_room_min_area.source: SANS 10400-C clause 4.2/4.4 (habitable room other than kitchen, scullery or laundry: 6 m2, no linear dimension < 2 m) - 2010 edition, re-verify against Ed. 3.01 (2016)
sans_room_min_area.finding: habitable room below the SANS 10400-C minimum size (no IRC equivalent is checked in this table)

sans_stair_riser_variation.source: SANS 10400-M clause 4.2 (variation in riser and going dimensions within a flight not more than 6 mm) - 2011 edition, re-verify against Ed. 3.02 (2025)
sans_stair_riser_variation.finding: riser/going variation within one flight exceeds the SANS 10400-M limit - a trip hazard and a common site defect

ceiling_min_mm.finding: habitable ceiling below the IRC minimum

sans.source: SANS 10400-C clause 4.3 (habitable room 2,4 m; passage/bathroom 2,1 m) - value taken from the 2010 edition per knowledge-base/03_codes_standards/02_sans-10400-parts-register.md; current is Ed. 3.01 (2016), RE-VERIFY against the purchased text before relying on it
sans.finding: habitable ceiling below the SANS 10400-C minimum (note: 2,4 m is 266 mm HIGHER than the IRC minimum - an IRC-compliant ceiling can fail here)

head_stack_geometry.source: pure geometry: opening head + lintel + structure depth must fit under floor-to-floor
head_stack_geometry.finding: opening head + structure exceeds the floor-to-floor height

window_fall_protection.source: IRC R312.2 (openable sill <610 mm above floor with >1830 mm drop outside requires guard/limiter)
window_fall_protection.finding: low openable sill over a high drop without fall protection

wet_wall_stacking.source: plumbing practice (stack wet walls between floors; drains near stacks)
wet_wall_stacking.finding: wet rooms on adjacent floors do not share a wall line - plumbing runs get long

cantilever_ratio.source: practice rule: cantilever beyond support flagged over back-span/4 (or > member depth for joists)
cantilever_ratio.finding: cantilever exceeds a quarter of its back-span

stacking_offset.source: practice rule: bearing wall above offset from wall below by more than the joist depth
stacking_offset.finding: upper bearing wall offset from lower support beyond the joist depth

prescriptive_scope_stories.source: IRC R101.2: the IRC's scope is one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses not more than three storeys above grade plane
prescriptive_scope_stories.finding: beyond the prescriptive envelope every rule in this report under-covers the building - rational design by a competent person is the applicable regime, not prescriptive tables

sans.source: SANS 10400-K deemed-to-satisfy masonry rules: empirical wall tables cover up to two storeys. RE-VERIFY the storey limit against the current SANS 10400-K edition text (encoded from the widely-stated empirical envelope, not from the paywalled standard itself)
